Title: October 12, 2023 - Boulder City Council Study Session

Topic1.Title: Opening Remarks and Community Statement on Middle East Events
Topic1.Summary: Council Member Juny Joseph opened the meeting and outlined the three agenda items and the meeting format. Council Member Tara Weiss, speaking in her individual capacity, expressed grief over the recent attacks in Israel, referenced Boulder's sister city Ra'anana and her work with Sustainable Israeli Palestinian Projects, and called for peace in the Middle East. Council Member Aaron Brockett noted that he had emailed Ra'anana's mayor to express personal and city support.

Topic2.Title: CAMP Access Management Plan Update
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented an evaluation of the Chautauqua Access Management Plan (CAMP), a program managing parking and shuttles at Chautauqua and the adjacent North Chautauqua neighborhood, which is set to sunset at the end of 2023. Results showed stable trail visitation, over 100,000 shuttle rides, and parking revenue exceeding shuttle operating costs, with strong stakeholder support for continuing the program. Staff recommended continuing CAMP with planned changes such as scooter access, a permanent B-cycle station, and updated signage, plus possible modifications including performance-based pricing, a commuter permit for employees, and using parking revenue for transportation demand management benefits. Staff also proposed a feasibility study on direct transit or microtransit access to Chautauqua and other trailheads, which Council supported, with concerns raised about equitable access and affordability for residents.

Topic3.Title: East Boulder Subcommunity Plan Zoning and Form-Based Code Implementation
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented an update on implementing the East Boulder Subcommunity Plan, focusing on a zoning and form-based code study for areas of change that are shifting from industrial to walkable mixed-use neighborhoods. Staff reviewed three completed form-based code projects in Boulder Junction and reported community and Planning Board feedback that the code can deliver quality design but may limit creativity, raise costs through building length and roof rules, and lack family-friendly outdoor space. Council members asked that the next phase reduce discretionary call-ups by making the process more prescriptive, reassess which rules are effective, allow more roof variety and iconic buildings where appropriate, and address the review process timeline. Staff will return in early 2024 with draft zoning and form-based code recommendations.

Topic4.Title: Support for Boulder County Ballot Measure 1A
Topic4.Summary: Council discussed a request to support Boulder County Ballot Measure 1A, a 0.5% sales and use tax extension that funds the purchase and maintenance of county open space. Council Member Aaron Brockett proposed adding the support to the consent agenda at the next business meeting. Council members unanimously expressed support for the measure.
